inline_comments.comment: The string-form `run` test asserts exact call counts (`toHaveBeenCalledTimes(2)`) for both `removeEntryFromArray` and `appendValueToArray`, but the object-form test (lines 241–248) asserts only the arguments, not the counts. If a regression caused the loop to iterate extra times or call the wrong method, this test would still pass. Add `expect(mocks.configFile.removeEntryFromArray).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` and `expect(mocks.configFile.appendValueToArray).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(1)` to match the rigour of the sibling test.

The changes to this file (and to `generateEntrypoint.test.ts`, `generateScripts.test.ts`, and `index.test.ts`) — adding `.ts` extensions to imports and reformatting `runMetroCodemodOrFallback` call sites to multi-line style — are unrelated to the on-device addons migration. Bundling cosmetic churn with a functional change makes the diff harder to review and future reverts harder to scope. These should be extracted into a separate cleanup PR.

general_comments.comment: The `prompt()` message is a static string that tells the user what category of addons was found, but doesn't name the specific packages detected (e.g., `@storybook/addon-ondevice-controls`). The `Fix` type defines `prompt` as `() => string` with no access to `result`, so the current implementation is correct within that contract. It is worth noting, however, that users running the migration interactively would benefit from seeing the actual package names in the prompt. If the `Fix` interface is ever extended to pass `result` into `prompt`, this would be a good first candidate to update.
